questions.question: What is the domain of $f(x) = \ln(x - 2) + \sqrt{9 - x}$?
questions.answer: The logarithm needs $x - 2 > 0$, so $x > 2$; the square root needs $9 - x \ge 0$, so $x \le 9$. Domain: $x > 2$ and $x \le 9$.

questions.question: What is the value of $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{20} -(-1)^r$?
questions.answer: The terms are $1, -1, 1, -1, \ldots, 1, -1$ (20 terms), which cancel in pairs, so the sum is $0$.

questions.question: The graph shows a normal distribution. Approximately 99.7% of the area under the curve is bounded by $x = 25$ and $x = 145$. What are the mean and variance that best represent this information?
questions.answer: 99.7% of the area lies within 3 standard deviations of the mean, so the mean is the midpoint $\mu = \dfrac{25 + 145}{2} = 85$ and $85 - 3\sigma = 25 \Rightarrow \sigma = 20$, so the variance is $400$.

questions.question: Which equation best represents the graph shown (defined for $x > 0$)?
questions.answer: The graph approaches the origin, so only A and B are possible ($y \to 0$ as $x \to 0$). The curve is flat at the origin, like a double root: $y = x^2(x + 1)$ has a double root at $x = 0$, while $y = 4x^2 + x$ has a single root there (non-zero gradient).

questions.question: The diagram shows a shaded region bounded by $y = f(x)$, $y = 0$, $x = 2a$ and $x = -2a$. Which of these expressions does NOT find the shaded area?
questions.answer:
$f$ is odd, so the region below the axis cancels the region above it: $\displaystyle\int_{-2a}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = 0$, which is not the area. The total area is $6a^2$ (each half is a triangle of area $a^2$ plus a rectangle of area $2a^2$), matching C ($2a^2 + 4a^2$) and D.

(Note: strictly, B evaluates to $-6a^2$, the negative of the area; the intended answer is A.)

What is the simplified form of $\cot(270^\circ + x)\cos(-x)$?
questions.answer: $\cot(270^\circ + x) = -\tan x$ and $\cos(-x) = \cos x$, so the expression is $-\tan x\cos x = -\sin x$.

questions.question: Let $h(x) = f(g(x))$, with $f(4) = 1$, $f'(x) = 6$, $g(2) = 4$ and $g'(2) = 4$. What is the equation of the tangent to the graph of $y = h(x)$ at $x = 2$?
Find the exact gradient of the tangent to the curve $y = \log_e(\tan x)$ at the point where $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
questions.answer:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\sec^2 x}{\tan x}.$$
At $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$: $\sec^2\dfrac{\pi}{3} = 4$ and $\tan\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \sqrt{3}$, so the gradient is $\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{3}}{3}$.

An arithmetic sequence, from start to end, is $51, 44, 37, \ldots, -47$. How many terms are there in the sequence?
questions.answer: $58 - 7n = -47 \Rightarrow 7n = 105 \Rightarrow n = 15$ terms.

Differentiate $y = e^x\tan(5x)$.
questions.answer: Product rule: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^x\tan(5x) + 5e^x\sec^2(5x)$.

questions.question: Differentiate $y = \log_e\left[\dfrac{x}{(x + 1)^4}\right]$.
questions.answer:
Using log laws, $y = \ln x - 4\ln(x + 1)$, so
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{x} - \frac{4}{x + 1} = \frac{1 - 3x}{x(x + 1)}.$$

questions.question:
A Ferris wheel has a diameter of 70 metres. Passengers board the carriages at the lowest point $P$, at ground level. The wheel rotates at a constant rate and completes one revolution every 20 minutes. Let $h$ be the height (in metres) of a carriage $t$ minutes after it passes $P$.

Find the height of the carriage after 5 minutes.
questions.answer: 5 minutes is a quarter of a revolution, so the carriage is level with the centre: $h = 35$ m.

questions.question:
A Ferris wheel has a diameter of 70 metres. Passengers board the carriages at the lowest point $P$, at ground level. The wheel rotates at a constant rate and completes one revolution every 20 minutes. Let $h$ be the height (in metres) of a carriage $t$ minutes after it passes $P$.

It is known that $h$ can be expressed in the form $h(t) = a\cos(bt) + c$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are constants. Find the values of $a$, $b$ and $c$.
questions.answer:
Period $\dfrac{2\pi}{b} = 20 \Rightarrow b = \dfrac{\pi}{10}$. The centre of the wheel is at height $c = 35$, the radius is 35 and $h(0) = 0$ (minimum), so $a = -35$.
$$h(t) = -35\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{10}\right) + 35.$$

questions.question:
A Ferris wheel has a diameter of 70 metres. Passengers board the carriages at the lowest point $P$, at ground level. The wheel rotates at a constant rate and completes one revolution every 20 minutes. Let $h$ be the height (in metres) of a carriage $t$ minutes after it passes $P$. The height is $h(t) = -35\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{10}\right) + 35$.

Sketch the graph of $h$ for $0 \le t \le 40$.
questions.answer: A cosine curve reflected in the $t$-axis, oscillating between $h = 0$ and $h = 70$, with minima at $t = 0, 20, 40$ and maxima of 70 at $t = 10, 30$.

questions.question:
A Ferris wheel has a diameter of 70 metres. Passengers board the carriages at the lowest point $P$, at ground level. The wheel rotates at a constant rate and completes one revolution every 20 minutes. Let $h$ be the height (in metres) of a carriage $t$ minutes after it passes $P$. The height is $h(t) = -35\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{10}\right) + 35$.

Let $R$ be the rate at which $h$ changes over time. By first finding $R$, find the maximum rate of change of $R$ with respect to time.
questions.answer:
$$R = h'(t) = \frac{7\pi}{2}\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{10}\right), \qquad \frac{dR}{dt} = \frac{7\pi^2}{20}\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{10}\right).$$
The maximum of $\dfrac{dR}{dt}$ is $\dfrac{7\pi^2}{20}$ m/min² (when $\cos\frac{\pi t}{10} = 1$).

questions.question:
A Ferris wheel has a diameter of 70 metres. Passengers board the carriages at the lowest point $P$, at ground level. The wheel rotates at a constant rate and completes one revolution every 20 minutes. Let $h$ be the height (in metres) of a carriage $t$ minutes after it passes $P$. The height is $h(t) = -35\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{10}\right) + 35$.

When Leo enters the carriage at $P$, he is excited to reach a height of 50 m above the ground. Determine how long it will take him to reach this height. Give your answer to the nearest second.
questions.answer:
$$50 = -35\cos\frac{\pi t}{10} + 35 \Rightarrow \cos\frac{\pi t}{10} = -\frac{3}{7} \Rightarrow t = \frac{10}{\pi}\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{3}{7}\right) \approx 6.41 \text{ min}.$$
That is 6 minutes 25 seconds.

When cooking oil cools, its temperature $T$ (°C) after $t$ minutes is given by $T = 60 + 150e^{-0.1t}$. What is the initial temperature of the oil?

When cooking oil cools, its temperature $T$ (°C) after $t$ minutes is given by $T = 60 + 150e^{-0.1t}$. At what temperature is the oil cooling at a rate of 10 °C per minute? Give your answer to the nearest degree.
questions.answer:
$\dfrac{dT}{dt} = -15e^{-0.1t} = -10 \Rightarrow e^{-0.1t} = \dfrac{2}{3}$ (so $t \approx 4.05$ min).
$$T = 60 + 150\times\frac{2}{3} = 160\ ^\circ\text{C}.$$

questions.question: When cooking oil cools, its temperature $T$ (°C) after $t$ minutes is given by $T = 60 + 150e^{-0.1t}$. What temperature does the oil eventually cool to?
questions.answer: As $t \to \infty$, $e^{-0.1t} \to 0$, so $T \to 60$ °C.

questions.question: Let $f(x) = x - 2$ and $g(x) = (x + 2)(x^2 - 4)$. Find the $x$-coordinates of all points of intersection of the graphs of $f(x)$ and $g(x)$.
questions.answer:
$$x - 2 = (x + 2)^2(x - 2) \Rightarrow (x - 2)\left[1 - (x + 2)^2\right] = 0.$$
So $x = 2$ or $(x + 2)^2 = 1 \Rightarrow x = -1$ or $x = -3$. Intersections at $x = -3, -1, 2$.

questions.question:
Let $f(x) = x - 2$ and $g(x) = (x + 2)(x^2 - 4)$. The graphs intersect at $x = -3, -1, 2$.

Sketch the graphs of $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ on the same axes, showing all important features, including the points of intersection. (Do not find any stationary points.)
questions.answer: $g(x) = (x + 2)^2(x - 2)$: a positive cubic with a double root (touching) at $x = -2$, a single root at $x = 2$ and $y$-intercept $-8$. The line $y = x - 2$ has intercepts $(2, 0)$ and $(0, -2)$. Points of intersection: $(-3, -5)$, $(-1, -3)$, $(2, 0)$.

questions.question:
Let $f(x) = x - 2$ and $g(x) = (x + 2)(x^2 - 4)$. The graphs intersect at $x = -3, -1, 2$.

Hence, or otherwise, solve the inequality $x - 2 < (x + 2)(x^2 - 4)$.
questions.answer: The cubic lies above the line for $-3 < x < -1$ or $x > 2$.

questions.question: The velocity $\dot{x}$ (m/s) of a particle moving in a horizontal straight line is $\dot{x} = 3 - \dfrac{9}{t - 2}$ for $t > 2$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. In which direction is the particle travelling when $t = 3$? Justify your answer.
questions.answer: At $t = 3$, $\dot x = 3 - 9 = -6 < 0$, so the particle is moving to the left (in the negative direction).

questions.question: The velocity $\dot{x}$ (m/s) of a particle moving in a horizontal straight line is $\dot{x} = 3 - \dfrac{9}{t - 2}$ for $t > 2$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. Find the time when the particle changes direction.
questions.answer: $3 - \dfrac{9}{t - 2} = 0 \Rightarrow t - 2 = 3 \Rightarrow t = 5$ s (the velocity changes sign there).

questions.question:
The velocity $\dot{x}$ (m/s) of a particle moving in a horizontal straight line is $\dot{x} = 3 - \dfrac{9}{t - 2}$ for $t > 2$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. The particle changes direction at $t = 5$.

Find the distance travelled by the particle between $t = 3$ and $t = 7$, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
$$\text{Distance} = -\int_3^5\left(3 - \frac{9}{t - 2}\right)dt + \int_5^7\left(3 - \frac{9}{t - 2}\right)dt$$
With $\displaystyle\int\left(3 - \frac{9}{t - 2}\right)dt = 3t - 9\ln(t - 2)$:
$$= -\left[(15 - 9\ln 3) - 9\right] + \left[(21 - 9\ln 5) - (15 - 9\ln 3)\right] = (9\ln 3 - 6) + \left(6 + 9\ln\tfrac{3}{5}\right) \approx 5.29 \text{ m}.$$

questions.question: Events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A) = \dfrac{3k}{4}$, $P(B) = k$ and $P(\overline{A} \cap B) = k^2$, where $0 < k < 1$. Find an expression for $P(A \cap B)$ in terms of $k$.
questions.answer: $P(A \cap B) = P(B) - P(\overline{A} \cap B) = k - k^2$.

questions.question: Events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A) = \dfrac{3k}{4}$, $P(B) = k$ and $P(\overline{A} \cap B) = k^2$, where $0 < k < 1$. Then $P(A \cap B) = k - k^2$. Given that $A$ and $B$ are independent, find the value of $k$.
questions.answer:
$P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$:
$$k - k^2 = \frac{3k}{4}\cdot k \Rightarrow 4k - 4k^2 = 3k^2 \Rightarrow k(7k - 4) = 0.$$
Since $0 < k < 1$, $k = \dfrac{4}{7}$.

Show that the amount remaining after the third monthly payment is
$$A_3 = 400\,000 \times 1.0025^3 - M\left(1 + 1.0025 + 1.0025^2\right).$$

Julio invests \$400 000 in an annuity that earns interest at 3% p.a. compounded monthly, and receives regular payments of \$$M$ at the end of each month. Let $A_n$ be the amount in the account after $n$ months. After $n$ months, $A_n = 400\,000 \times 1.0025^n - M\left(1 + 1.0025 + \cdots + 1.0025^{n-1}\right)$.

Determine the monthly payment Julio receives if the annuity is to last for 25 years.

The graph shows the function $y = f(x)$, which has a horizontal asymptote and points of inflection at $(-5, 0)$ and $(5, 0)$. Sketch the graph of $y = f'(x)$, clearly showing the behaviour at the intercepts and any asymptotes.
questions.answer:
- $f$ has a maximum turning point at $x = 0$, so $f'(0) = 0$ and $f'$ changes from positive to negative there.
- The points of inflection at $x = \pm 5$ are where the gradient is steepest, giving a maximum of $f'$ at $x = -5$ and a minimum at $x = 5$.
- As $x \to \pm\infty$, $f$ flattens towards its asymptote, so $f'(x) \to 0$: the $x$-axis is an asymptote of $f'$.

questions.question:
Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{3x}{4}(2 - x), & 0 \le x \le 2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$

Prove that $f(x)$ is a probability density function.
questions.answer:
$f(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$ (the parabola $\tfrac{3x}{4}(2 - x)$ is non-negative on $[0, 2]$, and $f = 0$ elsewhere), and
$$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx = \frac{3}{4}\int_0^2(2x - x^2)\,dx = \frac{3}{4}\left[x^2 - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = \frac{3}{4}\left(4 - \frac{8}{3}\right) = 1.$$
Hence $f$ is a probability density function.

questions.question: Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{3x}{4}(2 - x), & 0 \le x \le 2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$ State the mode of the distribution.
questions.answer: The maximum of $f$ is at the vertex $x = 1$, so the mode is $1$.

questions.question: Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{3x}{4}(2 - x), & 0 \le x \le 2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$ Find $P(X > 1.5)$.
Consider the function $f(x) = \log_e(x^2 + 1)$. Find the stationary point(s) of $f(x)$ and determine their nature.
Consider the function $f(x) = \log_e(x^2 + 1)$. Its second derivative is $f''(x) = \dfrac{2(1 - x^2)}{(x^2 + 1)^2}$. Find the coordinates of the point(s) of inflection of $f(x)$.
questions.answer:
$f''(x) = 0 \Rightarrow x = \pm 1$, with $f(\pm 1) = \ln 2$. Checking concavity: $f''(-2) = -\tfrac{6}{25} < 0$, $f''(0) = 2 > 0$, $f''(2) = -\tfrac{6}{25} < 0$, so the concavity changes at both points.

Points of inflection: $(-1, \ln 2)$ and $(1, \ln 2)$.

questions.question:
Consider the function $f(x) = \log_e(x^2 + 1)$. It has a minimum turning point at $(0, 0)$ and points of inflection at $(\pm 1, \ln 2)$.

Sketch the curve $y = f(x)$, showing all key features.
questions.answer: An even function with minimum $(0, 0)$, concave up for $-1 < x < 1$, points of inflection at $(\pm 1, \ln 2)$, and concave down for $|x| > 1$, increasing without bound as $x \to \pm\infty$.

questions.question: Use the trapezoidal rule with four subintervals to find an approximation to $\displaystyle\int_1^3 \log_e(x^2 + 1)\,dx$.

Consider the function $f(x) = \log_e(x^2 + 1)$. It is concave up for $-1 < x < 1$ and concave down for $|x| > 1$. The trapezoidal rule with four subintervals gives $\displaystyle\int_1^3 \ln(x^2 + 1)\,dx \approx 3.1335$.

State whether this approximation is greater or less than the exact value, with a brief justification.
questions.answer: Less than. On $1 \le x \le 3$ the curve is concave down, so each straight-line chord used by the trapezoidal rule lies below the curve, and the trapezoids underestimate the area.

questions.question: The graph shows a shaded region bounded by $y^2 = 2x + 6$ and $y = x - 1$. Find the area of the region.
questions.answer:
Write both in terms of $y$: $x = \dfrac{y^2 - 6}{2}$ and $x = y + 1$. Intersections: $\dfrac{y^2 - 6}{2} = y + 1 \Rightarrow y^2 - 2y - 8 = 0 \Rightarrow y = 4, -2$, i.e. $(5, 4)$ and $(-1, -2)$.
$$A = \int_{-2}^{4}\left[(y + 1) - \frac{y^2 - 6}{2}\right]dy = \int_{-2}^{4}\left(-\frac{y^2}{2} + y + 4\right)dy = \left[-\frac{y^3}{6} + \frac{y^2}{2} + 4y\right]_{-2}^{4}$$
$$= \frac{40}{3} - \left(-\frac{14}{3}\right) = 18 \text{ units}^2.$$

questions.question: The graph shows $y = f'(x)$, which crosses the $x$-axis at point $A$, has a minimum turning point at $B$ and has the asymptote $y = 0$. It is known that $y = f(x)$ also has an asymptote at $y = 0$. Sketch a possible graph of $y = f(x)$, showing all important features and marking the points $A'$ and $B'$ corresponding to $A$ and $B$.
questions.answer:
- At $A$, $f'$ changes from positive to negative, so $A'$ is a local **maximum** of $f$.
- At $B$, $f'$ has a minimum, so $f''$ changes sign: $B'$ is a point of inflection (not horizontal, since $f'(B) < 0$).
- As $x \to \infty$, $f' \to 0^-$ and $f$ decreases towards its asymptote $y = 0$ from above.

questions.question:
The table gives values of $P(Z < z)$ for the standard normal distribution.

Maya is training for the long jump. To compete at the national age championships, her longest jump must be beaten by less than 0.26% of the general population. The distance jumped by the general population is normally distributed with mean 3.48 m and standard deviation 1.08 m. Using the table, find the minimum distance Maya needs to jump, correct to the nearest centimetre.
questions.answer:
We need $P(X > x) = 0.0026$, i.e. $P(Z < z) = 0.9974$. From the table, $z \approx 2.8$.
$$2.8 = \frac{x - 3.48}{1.08} \Rightarrow x = 3.48 + 3.024 = 6.504 \approx 6.50 \text{ m}.$$

questions.question:
Emma is plane-spotting at a sea-level point $E$. She can see her house $H$ on a bearing of 030°T, and a plane $A$ directly above her house at an angle of elevation of 20°. From $A$, the plane travels at a constant altitude of 900 m on a bearing of 225°T to a point $B$, 1700 m away, which is directly above a landmark $L$.

Determine the bearing and the angle of elevation of the aircraft at $B$ from Emma's position $E$.
questions.answer:
In $\triangle EHA$: $EH = \dfrac{900}{\tan 20^\circ} \approx 2472.73$ m.

In $\triangle EHL$ (at ground level, $HL = 1700$): the bearing of $E$ from $H$ is 210° and of $L$ from $H$ is 225°, so $\angle EHL = 15^\circ$.
$$EL^2 = 1700^2 + 2472.73^2 - 2(1700)(2472.73)\cos 15^\circ \Rightarrow EL \approx 939.99 \text{ m}.$$
Angle of elevation of $B$: $\tan\alpha = \dfrac{900}{939.99} \Rightarrow \alpha \approx 44^\circ$.

Bearing: in $\triangle EHL$, $\dfrac{\sin\beta}{1700} = \dfrac{\sin 15^\circ}{939.99}$ where $\beta = \angle HEL$, giving $\beta \approx 27.9^\circ$ (acute, since it is not opposite the longest side). The bearing of $L$ (and $B$) from $E$ is $30^\circ - 27.9^\circ \approx 002^\circ$T.

questions.question: Given $n$ is a constant, simplify $\displaystyle\int x^n(1 + x)^n\left(1 + \frac{1}{x}\right)^n dx$.
questions.answer:
$x^n\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^n = (x + 1)^n$, so
$$\int x^n(1 + x)^n\left(1 + \frac{1}{x}\right)^n dx = \int (1 + x)^{2n}\,dx = \frac{(1 + x)^{2n + 1}}{2n + 1} + C \quad (n \ne -\tfrac{1}{2}).$$

questions.question:
Helen practises on a three-leg course from $S$ to $F$ (see diagram). She swims in a straight line from $S$ to a point $X$ on the straight road $OY$, rides along the road from $X$ to $Y$, then jogs from $Y$ to $F$ around a quarter-circle path of radius 2 km. The perpendicular distance from $S$ to $O$ is 2 km and $OY = 4$ km. She swims at 4 km/h, rides at 16 km/h and jogs at 8 km/h. Let $OX = a$ km.

Show that the time $T$ hours to complete the course is $T = \dfrac{4\sqrt{a^2 + 4} - a + (4 + 2\pi)}{16}$.
questions.answer:
Swim: $SX = \sqrt{a^2 + 4}$, time $\dfrac{\sqrt{a^2 + 4}}{4}$. Ride: $XY = 4 - a$, time $\dfrac{4 - a}{16}$. Jog: quarter circle of radius 2, length $\tfrac{2\pi\times 2}{4} = \pi$, time $\dfrac{\pi}{8}$.
$$T = \frac{\sqrt{a^2 + 4}}{4} + \frac{4 - a}{16} + \frac{\pi}{8} = \frac{4\sqrt{a^2 + 4} - a + (4 + 2\pi)}{16}.$$

questions.question:
Helen practises on a three-leg course from $S$ to $F$ (see diagram). She swims in a straight line from $S$ to a point $X$ on the straight road $OY$, rides along the road from $X$ to $Y$, then jogs from $Y$ to $F$ around a quarter-circle path of radius 2 km. The perpendicular distance from $S$ to $O$ is 2 km and $OY = 4$ km. She swims at 4 km/h, rides at 16 km/h and jogs at 8 km/h. Let $OX = a$ km. The total time is $T = \dfrac{4\sqrt{a^2 + 4} - a + (4 + 2\pi)}{16}$ hours.

Find the value of $a$ that minimises the time taken to complete the course.
questions.answer:
$$\frac{dT}{da} = \frac{1}{16}\left(\frac{4a}{\sqrt{a^2 + 4}} - 1\right) = 0 \Rightarrow 4a = \sqrt{a^2 + 4} \Rightarrow 15a^2 = 4 \Rightarrow a = \frac{2}{\sqrt{15}} \approx 0.52 \text{ km}.$$
Test: at $a = 0.5$, $\dfrac{dT}{da} \approx \dfrac{1}{16}(0.970 - 1) < 0$; at $a = 0.6$, $\dfrac{dT}{da} \approx \dfrac{1}{16}(1.149 - 1) > 0$. So $a = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{15}}$ km gives the minimum time.
